items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: You had Sherwood, Dr. Bob Barber, Naki, Paul Crawford, there. What do you think of that session?

ctx.x: and he has to get his practice in every day or he gets nervous. And of course, the thing that he's doing is so extremely demanding that I can imagine that it doesn't take much to get out of practice with the business of trying to reproduce literally the sound of Jelly Roll Morton. He works with that variable speed tape recorder, which he regulates the speed of to provide the right pitch. Then he plays the Jelly Roll records, and then he plays the piano, you see. And he's never through until you can only hear one…

I've got about one minute. I don't know that we can really get into the things, but we were talking. While we were on these particular people, you had the lakefront lounges there. You had Sherwood, Dr. Bob Barber, Naki, Paul Crawford, there. What do you think of that session?

I think that's a fine session. That's one of the big kicks that I have to recall is the making of that session. It was a pretty freewheeling session, and I felt that we did a lot of very original material there. We had an original approach to things, and I think everybody liked it.
